title: Call Us Dropdown
description:
The contact-number disclosure on the safari expert panel — the copy of live's `li.call-cta.dropdown`. Applied to a `core/accordion` holding one `core/accordion-item`, whose panel contains the `dropdown-call-us` template part. Used by patterns/safari-expert.php.

⚠️ **The header no longer uses this variation.** On 2026-08-27 the header's Call Us became an `ollie/mega-menu` inside a `core/navigation` carrying `is-style-call-us-navigation` — hover-open, with the pop-out built by the plugin instead of argued out of the flow here. This variation now has exactly one placement: the safari expert panel, patterns/safari-expert.php.

It keeps the accordion deliberately. `ollie/mega-menu` declares `"parent": ["core/navigation"]`, so using it there would put a navigation landmark inside a per-post content panel — wrong for an in-flow disclosure with no menu semantics, and it would make a `wp_navigation` post a dependency of a template that renders per post. → styles/blocks/navigation/call-us-navigation.json

Everything below that reads as being about the header is kept as the record of why the swap was worth making — the pop-out declarations, the 110px→355px specificity bug, the heading-level type leak. None of it is live any more.

## Why this is a core accordion and not a block

It was `sd/call-us` until 2026-08-21 — a plugin block that emitted a `<button>`, a panel and the ARIA wiring between them, and nothing else. WordPress 7.1 ships that: `core/accordion-heading` renders a real `<button class="wp-block-accordion-heading__toggle">` that resets the UA button styling and inherits type, `core/accordion` carries the chevron and the `autoclose` behaviour, and the open/close state runs through the Interactivity API in @wordpress/block-library/accordion/view — toggled by `hidden="until-found"` on the panel and `.is-open` on the item, so there is no inline height animation to fight.

That swap is what made this file possible. `sd/call-us` was a non-core block, and assets/styles/sd-call-us.css opened by explaining why it had to be 300 lines of CSS: `styles.blocks` reaches only a block's own wrapper, and every part that needed styling — the toggle, the panel, the rows — was a descendant of it with no JSON home. Every one of those is now a block in its own right, so it has one. What is left in assets/styles/core-accordion.css is four things this format genuinely cannot express, listed at the top of that file.

It also retired three class hooks: `.sd-call-us__toggle`, `.sd-call-us__panel` and `.sd-call-us__number`, plus the `.sd-call-us--start` / `--end` placement pair and the `.sd-header__call-us` and `.sd-expert__call` instance hooks. Nothing authored carries an `sd-*` class for this component now.

## The closed panel has to be `display: none`

The Interactivity API closes the panel with `hidden="until-found"`, and that value does **not** mean `display: none`. The HTML rendering spec is `[hidden]:not([hidden=until-found]){display:none}` plus `[hidden=until-found]{content-visibility:hidden}` — so the panel's *box* went on rendering with its ground, border, radius and shadow, and because it is absolutely positioned 8px below the trigger it read as a white bar under the closed accordion. Seen on local 2026-08-21. The `[hidden]` rule in the `css` field below is the fix.

The cost is `beforematch`: `until-found` exists so in-page find and hash links can open a closed panel, and `display: none` takes that away. It is the right trade here — these are four phone numbers in a header, not page content anyone searches for with Ctrl+F — but it would be the wrong one in a FAQ accordion, so do not copy this rule into a section style without re-reading this note.

## The pop-out

The panel's `spacing.margin` is zeroed, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy-up. It is a flow child of the accordion item, so theme.json's global block gap reaches it as `:root :where(.is-layout-flow) > *{margin-block-start:var(--wp--preset--spacing--60)}` — and a margin on an absolutely positioned box is added to its inset, so the panel hung ~50px below where `inset-block-start: calc(100% + 8px)` put it, detached from the trigger and floating over the page below the header. Measured on local 2026-08-27. Do not reintroduce a vertical margin here; pad the panel instead.

An accordion panel is in flow — it pushes what follows it down, which is right in a FAQ and wrong in a header bar. The four declarations that lift it out are in the `css` field below, and they are the whole cost of using an accordion here.

Alignment is the panel's inline start, and that is now the only case — the safari expert panel's button sits at the left of a flex row. The `is-style-header` flip that used to sit alongside it in core-accordion.css went with the header.

## What changed from live, and why

Live draws the panel as a hard-edged rectangle — `#fff`, a 1px `#ccc` border, no radius, no shadow — butted flush against the trigger, and gives the label and the number the same weight and colour. Zared asked for the same content in a softer container, so: a 200 radius and a 300 shadow, both presets, so the panel reads as floating rather than welded to the bar; 8px of clearance under the button, affordable because this opens on click where live's expert-panel copy opens on hover; and the label dropped to neutral-600 so the number is what the eye lands on. The rows' hairlines and hover tint are in core-accordion.css.

The number does *not* underline on row hover. The tint already says the row is live, and underlining the number on top of it makes a four-row list flicker as the pointer crosses it. `:focus` still underlines, because a keyboard user gets the tint from `:focus-within` on the row and needs the link itself identified as well.

Everything else is live's: the numbers, their labels, the flags, and the order.

## The pop-out declarations are `!important`, and they have to be

WordPress compiles a block style variation's `css` field into
`:root :where(<selector>)`, which lands at specificity **(0,1,0)** — `:root`
contributes the whole of it and `:where()` contributes nothing. That is low
enough to lose a *tie on source order* to any equally-specific `position`
declaration that happens to load later, and on dev it does.

The symptom, reported 2026-08-27 and reproduced exactly: with the panel open the
header grew from 110px to 355px. `position` computed as `relative` instead of
`absolute`, so the panel stayed in flow — the utility row went to 295px, the
enquiry button stretched to match it, the logo and Trustpilot mark centred
themselves in a 295px band, and the nav was pushed down onto the hero. And
because `inset-block-start: calc(100% + 8px)` is a *relative offset* once
`position` is `relative`, the panel itself was displaced 303px down its own flow
position and hung over the navigation. Confirmed by injecting one rule —
`.wp-block-accordion-panel{position:relative}` — into an otherwise untouched dev
page and matching the reported screenshots pixel for pixel.

It appeared only for logged-in users, which is what made it look
environment-specific rather than a specificity bug: dev serves logged-in requests
uncached and with the admin bar's stylesheet stack on top, and that is enough to
change which side of the tie loses. Anonymous requests to the same URL measured
110px at every width tested.

So the four declarations that lift the panel out of flow — `position`,
`inset-block-start`, `inset-inline-start` and `z-index` — are marked, along with
`position: relative` on the accordion itself, which is the positioning context
they resolve against and is equally exposed at (0,1,0).

This is the same reasoning, and the same remedy, as
styles/blocks/navigation/main-navigation.json: "!important throughout because
WordPress wraps a block style's css in :root :where() at specificity (0,1,0)".
`min-width` and `text-align` are left unmarked — nothing contests them, and if
something ever does the failure is cosmetic rather than structural.

## Not carried here — but made to arrive

The trigger's own weight, colour and size. The header wants brand-500 at font-size 200 and bold, the expert panel wants inherited colour at 200 and semi-bold — so those travel on each block instance, where they are visible in the editor. `core/accordion` serialises `typography.fontWeight` properly, which `sd/call-us` did not: its render callback dropped the style-engine output and the attribute silently rendered at 400, which is why the old stylesheet set the weight from a class.

What this file does carry is the one declaration that lets those instance attributes reach the button at all: `core/accordion-heading` is set to `font-size: inherit` and `font-weight: inherit`. Core's `.wp-block-accordion-heading__toggle` already inherits everything, but the block it inherits *from* is a heading — `<h3>` in the header, `<h4>` on the expert panel — and this theme styles both through `styles.elements`. So the heading level was silently deciding the trigger's type: the header's label rendered at 24px semi-bold (h3: font-size 400) rather than the authored 300 bold, and below about 1100px that 24px label wrapped inside a `flexWrap: nowrap` cluster and collided with the Trustpilot mark. Both instances rendered at a size nobody had chosen. Measured on local 2026-08-27.

The header's trigger is **font-size 300** — Zared's decision, 2026-08-27, confirmed after this file had briefly argued for 200 on the grounds that live's label measures 18px and 300 is 19.2px fluid to 24px. It is 300. Do not "correct" it to 200 again: the size is approved, and the wrap it used to cause below ~1024px is fixed where it belongs, with `white-space: nowrap` on the toggle in assets/styles/core-accordion.css, rather than by shrinking the type.

The rule worth remembering: on any block whose wrapper is a heading, an `elements.h*` style outranks the block's own font-size attribute. `inherit` is what hands control back to the instance.
